3. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.181/2021, under Sections 498A/406/506/323/34 IPC & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, registered at Police Station Gokulpuri,
Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 30.11.2017 according to Hindu rites and This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/10/2023 at 21:30:16 ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
Out of the said wedlock, a male child was born on 14.08.2019.
After the marriage, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 06.05.2019.
On 05.08.2021, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement dated 24.05.2022 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13-B(2) of the HMA Act was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree of divorce dated 01.02.2023 passed by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, North-East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Court, North-East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi

sentences.text: The copy of the decree is already on record.
6. All the petitioners and respondent no. 2 appeared through video- conferencing.
Parties have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with them and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.

She submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion and further submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them, and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
7. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/10/2023 at 21:30:16 8.
Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.181/2021,
under Sections 498A/406/506/323/34 IPC & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, registered at Police Station Gokulpuri, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.

However,
the rights of the child born from the wedlock of petitioner no. 1 and respondent no.2 are left open to be adjudicated by him/her as and when he/she attains majority as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava & Ors, decided on 22.04.2019 in Civil Appeal Nos.4031-4032 of 2019.
9. The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J OCTOBER 17, 2023/akc
